title: China's Xi Jinping pays tribute to ex-leader Jiang Zemin, architect of the post-Tiananmen crackdown
subhead: President Xi Jinping used the centenary of former Chinese Communist Party leader Jiang Zemin's birth to praise his toughness after the crackdown on the June 1989 student movement and recall the golden age of China's economy.

subhead: A deeply religious Romanian evangelical family, newly settled in a small Norwegian town, clashes with the country's liberal principles and ultimately the courts when the couple is suspected of child abuse.

subhead: 'Voices of Afghan Women' (3/6). Radio Begum, 'a radio station made by women for women,' is the only connection to the outside world for many Afghan women. It is one of several projects to help young girls access education under the Taliban regime.

title: Mahmoud Darwish and Tamar Ben Ami: The impossible love of a Palestinian poet and an Israeli dancer
subhead: In the early 1960s, in Haifa, Israel, the young Palestinian poet Mahmoud Darwish fell in love with Tamar Ben Ami, a Jewish Israeli dancer. Their romance was intense but brief. From this forbidden love, the writer composed a poignant poem, 'Rita and the Rifle,' which is still sung throughout the Arab world.

title: Why Le Pen's plan for a constitutional referendum would be 'a coup d'état in form and content'
subhead: If she were to win, far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen has pledged to call a referendum to revise the Constitution and enshrine the far right's core principles in it. According to a member of the highest administrative court, this would be 'a double coup d'état, both in form and content.'
